correctness.rationale: For n>=3 the crown distance table is exact: same-part distinct pairs distance 2, matching nonedges distance 3, other cross pairs distance 1. Same-part difference profiles force every doubly resolving set to omit at most one matched pair P_i, yielding |S|>=n-1. For a single omitted P_i, its matched endpoints require landmarks on both sides. An adjacent cross pair a_i,b_j (i!=j) has just two +/-1 difference levels, each a matched-pair transversal. A set of n-1 vertices is one-hole transversal, and avoids every level exactly if >=3 vertices are chosen from each side. This is feasible precisely for n>=7. For 3<=n<=6 any optimum n-set either has one omitted and another doubled pair (automatically defeats all transversals) or is a full transversal excluding B-side weights 2 and n-2. Counting gives all exact stated coefficients. Independent verifier enumerates all subsets through the claimed optimum for n=3..9, with 142924 subset checks, zero classification mismatches, and bases n3..9 = 14,58,172,514,140,560,1638. The infinite theorem is proved by the distance-level case analysis, not bounded experiments.

originality.rationale: Originality is a best-of-knowledge judgment for the all-n crown vertex-doubly-resolving phase transition, exact minimum-set structure and enumerations. Foundational theory and general bounds do not imply it; related same-invariant complete multipartite and chain graph theorems exclude the matching-deleted crown; the crown edge-metric theorem is a distinct statistic. Finite cases that follow from classical cycle or hypercube results are not claimed as novel. Searches are not proof of absence and residual unindexed priority risks remain.

The simple local distance-level argument might exist as folklore or in unindexed computational appendices; no historical priority guarantee is asserted.
Classical C6 and hypercube special cases are not independently novel; contribution is the uniform all-n and all-bases statement.

self_review.scientific_scope: The earlier mathematical review assessed the same n>=3 crown theorem and its matched-pair and transversal proof. This independent review rechecked the claim and sources anew; no external certification is asserted.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are canonical distance-three matching-deleted complete bipartite graphs. The exact vertex doubly-resolving invariant is mathematically motivated by landmark localization and the classical relation to Cartesian-product metric dimension. The theorem does not just recompute a known scalar: it gives a sharp parameter transition at n=7, complete structure of every minimum set and exact counts, with a nontrivial three-per-side constraint distinguishing doubly resolving from edge resolving. Such detailed bases are reusable as witnesses/counterexamples and for design of landmark sets. The classification is naturally an infinite-parameter family rather than an arbitrary tiny slice.
